source.title: Momentum effects in the cryptocurrency market after one-day abnormal returns

hypothesis: When an ongoing UTC day's return becomes abnormally large relative to the asset's prior daily-return distribution, the price continues in the same direction until the end of that UTC day.
mechanism: The source documents short-lived momentum after extreme one-day moves and explicitly proposes entering in the abnormal-return direction once the dynamic threshold is crossed and exiting at day end.
daily_return_definition: UTC day open-to-prior-completed-hour close. Dynamic threshold uses mean and standard deviation of the previous 60 completed UTC daily open-to-close returns only.
entry: At hourly close t, if cumulative current-day return first crosses mean +/- k*std, schedule position in that direction for next hourly open t+1. No trade if next open is a new UTC day.
exit: Flatten at the first open of the next UTC day.
universe: Point-in-time assets with at least 60 completed daily observations and top 80 percent by lagged trailing 30-day close*volume at decision time; minimum 5 eligible assets. Only triggered assets receive weight.
construction: Equal-weight across active triggered assets, total gross exposure 1.0. No leverage above 1x gross.
development_gate: Canonical base-cost net Sharpe > 0.70, positive net total return, at least 100 triggered asset-days, and at least 2 of 3 preregistered k variants have positive development return.
limitations: The source calibrated k by asset/sample size and focused on BTC/ETH/LTC; this broad-panel test preregisters one common k surface to avoid per-asset tuning. Funding is unavailable.
